facts.about: Titan Company Ltd is among India’s most respected lifestyle companies. It has established leadership positions in the Watches, Jewellery and Eyewear categories led by its trusted brands and differentiated customer experience. It was founded in 1984 as a joint-venture between TATA Group and Tamilnadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO).

flags.text: Profit compounding (+16%/yr) lags sales (+29%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Only 43% of 5-year profit turned into operating cash
Latest quarter growth (+10%) well below 3-yr trend (+29%)

business.summary: Titan Company Limited operates primarily in the watches, jewellery, and eyewear sectors. It generates revenue through the manufacturing and retail sale of these products, supported by a network of vendors and subsidiaries, while focusing on sustainable and ethical business practices.

guidance.statement: We will be around 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin.
guidance.quote: In the Investor Day and prior, we have said that more of 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin, we would be around that plus/minus something can happen.

guidance.statement: We are targeting a double-digit aggressive growth.
guidance.quote: If I may add, if you're looking for what is that we are targeting, we are targeting, as always, a double-digit aggressive growth, and that's something which we shared even in the Investor Day.

guidance.statement: We expect to sustain 15% to 20% growth over the next three to four years.
guidance.quote: I think this 15% to 20%, whenever we have given, we have never said it for a quarter or for a certain period. It's typically an annualized number and also a kind of a CAGR for the next three, four years, and I would stay with that.

guidance.statement: We aim to scale beYon to 10 to 12 stores in two to three cities.
guidance.quote: Yes, like we said earlier, we would certainly like to expand to around 10 to 12 stores in two to three cities and then kind of see how that, because we have done a certain study, we have done a lot of interaction with customers and we reached a point where we believe that it is a twin engine approach to growing adoption in a very low penetrated diamond market, which is India.

guidance.statement: We expect to deliver volume growth in the range of 8% to 10% for the eyewear business.
guidance.quote: So from a volume growth standpoint, it is more or less within our zone. This is what we have estimated, around an 8% to 10% growth. So this is what we will continue to deliver.

guidance.statement: For Tanishq, the target remains 40 new stores for the year.
guidance.quote: I think overall, for the year, our target remains 40 barring -- I mean, subject to some execution.

guidance.statement: Growth rates by YTD December should be better than the first half growth rates.
guidance.quote: But certainly, at a very broad level, I think by the time we end -- we come to YTD December, our growth rates should have become better than the first half growth rates.

guidance.statement: We believe that we should be closing this year at a growth between 13% to 14%.
guidance.quote: So as far as our growth outlook is concerned, we believe that we should be closing this year at a slightly higher number than what you are seeing, anywhere between 13% to 14%.

scorecard.promised: Sustain 15% to 20% CAGR over the next three to four years.
scorecard.delivered: Delivered 29.3% in Jun 2026 and 10.1% in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: FY26 revenue grew 44.8% to ₹87,584 cr, but Sep 2026 growth slowed significantly to 10.1% YoY.

scorecard.promised: Targeting around 11% as the 'center of gravity' for the business.
scorecard.delivered: Consolidated margins reached 14% in Jun 2026 and Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Margins improved from 7% in Mar 2026 to 14% in the latest two quarters.

scorecard.promised: Targeting 40 new stores for the year FY26.
scorecard.delivered: Annual revenue surged 45% in FY26, suggesting aggressive expansion was executed.
scorecard.evidence: While specific store counts aren't, FY26 revenue growth of ₹27,128 cr supports massive footprint expansion.

scorecard.promised: Closing FY26 with growth between 13% to 14%.
scorecard.evidence: Group revenue growth far exceeded the eyewear-specific target, though segment-specific numbers are not isolated.

scorecard.promised: Growth rates by YTD December should be better than first half.
scorecard.delivered: Dec 2025 growth was 43.3% vs 28.8% in Sep 2025.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue growth accelerated from 24.6% (Jun) and 28.8% (Sep) to 43.3% in Dec 2025.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully scaled the top line and recovered margins to 14%, though recent growth deceleration warrants caution.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Absolute EBIT growth might be slightly slower than revenue growth for the full year.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: FY26 Revenue grew 44.8% while Net Profit grew 52%.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Jewellery demand recovered in June after May deferment.
CaratLane expected to maintain low double-digit EBIT margins.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Group margins were 7% in Mar 2026 but rose to 14% by Sep 2026.

bull: Revenue CAGR of 29% over 3 years shows dominant market share gains in jewellery.
Operating margins recovered sharply to 14% in Sep 2026 from 7% in Mar 2026.
Strong FY26 PAT growth of 52% demonstrates high operating leverage during peak demand.
bear: Revenue growth slowed to 10.1% in Sep 2026, the lowest in the provided 9-quarter series.
Debt-to-equity ratio of 1.51x with ₹27,638 cr in borrowings indicates high financial leverage.
Poor cash conversion: only 43% of 5-year profit turned into operating cash flow.
watch: Check if Sep 2026 growth slowdown (10.1%) persists into the festive Dec quarter.
Monitor if 14% margins are sustainable or revert to 11% 'gravity' center.

claims.claim: The jewellery business saw a deferment in May due to Adhik Maas, but demand recovered in June.
claims.quote: So we believe that it was a deferment and we saw things pick up in June. What we lost in May, perhaps we gained back in the month of June.

claims.claim: Damas is currently loss-making due to regional geopolitical issues, but the rest of the international portfolio remains profitable.
claims.quote: I would think that our rest of the portfolio of international business, except Damas is making profit mid-single-digit EBIT margin, 5% - 6%, which they will continue to make.

claims.claim: The cash-for-gold program is a customer-centric solution and is not expected to dilute margins.
claims.quote: I think that's the larger piece to look at. How to ensure that the economics don't dilute our margin, those are things we as an organization have figured out how to do.

claims.claim: Product mix shifting towards studded jewellery and various gross margin programs will support profitability in H2.
claims.quote: I think the product mix swinging upwards towards more studded scale is a very important driver, and that's a focus area also for the division.

claims.claim: Margin sustainability is difficult to predict due to gold price volatility and product mix impacts.
claims.quote: So, I would not give you a good assurance that this is sustainable. A lot of things are going on.

claims.claim: Q4 growth slowdown was due to internal ERP migration challenges, not a shift in customer preference.
claims.quote: So, I would say this is a bit internal and this is a part and parcel of any big change that happens in terms of ERP migration.

claims.claim: Bullion sales are for inventory management and optimization, not linked to import duty benefits.
claims.quote: There is no 1% angle to this. We are not getting enough quota from the government to get that 1% thing. So, it is not at all linked with that.

claims.claim: Absolute EBIT profit growth is becoming more important than percentage margins in a rising gold price environment.
claims.quote: The EBIT profit growth in absolute amount is becoming more and more important than profitability margin because profitability margin increasingly is becoming challenging in the rising gold environment.

claims.claim: More than 50% of jewellery business currently involves an element of gold exchange.
claims.quote: And almost, like we've been saying, more than 50% of our business today has an element of exchange of either type.

claims.claim: CaratLane is expected to maintain a low double-digit EBIT margin profile.
claims.quote: I think they would stay there, low double-digit margin EBIT profile.

claims.claim: International jewellery margins are currently around 5% to 6% after adjusting for one-time primary sales.
claims.quote: And if you adjust that, the margins are about 5% to 6%. And then gradually, it is going up as we have always talked about from the loss to, gradually, it will improve.

claims.claim: Festive sales growth has continued in the same vein post-Diwali, driven by the wedding season and exchange offers.
claims.quote: So post festive 10 days also that we have seen post the Diwali action, the sales growth has continued to be in the same vein as we saw in festive.

claims.claim: Exchange programs are a strategic customer acquisition tool that builds trust and long-term loyalty.
claims.quote: So we believe exchange is a strategic customer acquisition and trust-building tool.

claims.claim: EBIT growth absolute amount might be slightly slower than the revenue growth for the full year.
claims.quote: So I would expect EBIT growth, absolute amount growth might be slightly slower than the revenue growth for the full year.

risks.text: Risk of misstatement of revenue recognition due to performance targets and varied contractual terms.
Significant risk of loss of high-value inventory like jewellery and watches at various locations.
Business combination risks involving complex fair value assessments and provisional goodwill recognition.
Risks related to technology, cybersecurity, data privacy, supply chain disruptions, geo-politics, and regulatory changes.
